post.caption: Ground malachite painted Egyptian eyelids green. Egyptians used it as eye paint roughly 6,000 years ago. The name comes from the Greek word for mallow, a green plant. It forms above copper deposits, so it guided prospectors. Its bands record changing water as the stone grew. The most prized pattern is rounded rings like eyes. It is soft, about 3.5 to 4 on the Mohs scale. Big Russian malachite pieces were veneers of thin matched sheets. Saint Isaac's Cathedral in Saint Petersburg has ten malachite columns. Scientists tested Gutenberg Bibles with a laser and found malachite green.
